subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
intro: Each problem below uses a single step: one conversion, or one multiply, divide, add, or subtract where the resulting coefficient is already between $1$ and $10$. Write every answer in scientific notation $a \times 10^{n}$ with $1 \le a < 10$, unless the problem asks for standard form.

steps: Move the decimal point left until one nonzero digit remains in front of it: $5.2$
Count the places moved: from $52000.$ to $5.2$ is $4$ places to the left, so the exponent is $4$.
The number is large, so the exponent is positive: $5.2 \times 10^{4}$.
Move the decimal point right until one nonzero digit is in front of it: $9$
Count the places moved: from $0.0009$ to $9.0$ is $4$ places to the right.
The number is small (less than $1$), so the exponent is negative: $9 \times 10^{-4}$.
A positive exponent of $5$ means move the decimal point $5$ places to the right.
Start with $3.4$ and move right: $3.4 \to 340000.$, filling in zeros as needed.
A negative exponent of $-3$ means move the decimal point $3$ places to the left.
Start with $7.1$ and move left: $7.1 \to 0.0071$, filling in zeros as needed.

items.prompt: Compute $(2 \times 10^{3})(4 \times 10^{2})$. Write your answer in scientific notation.

steps: Combine: $8 \times 10^{5}$. The coefficient $8$ is already between $1$ and $10$, so no re-normalizing is needed.

items.prompt: Compute $(3 \times 10^{4})(3 \times 10^{1})$. Write your answer in scientific notation.
Compute $\dfrac{8 \times 10^{6}}{2 \times 10^{2}}$. Write your answer in scientific notation.
Compute $\dfrac{9 \times 10^{5}}{3 \times 10^{3}}$. Write your answer in scientific notation.
Compute $(5.1 \times 10^{4}) + (2.3 \times 10^{4})$. Write your answer in scientific notation.

steps: The powers of $10$ are the same ($10^{4}$), so add the coefficients directly.

items.prompt: Compute $(6.8 \times 10^{3}) - (2.5 \times 10^{3})$. Write your answer in scientific notation.

steps: The powers of $10$ match ($10^{3}$), so subtract the coefficients directly.

Compute $\dfrac{6 \times 10^{2}}{3 \times 10^{5}}$. Write your answer in scientific notation.
